_comment: STILL image generation (studio headshots and portraits).
Hand this whole file to the image model, or paste one of the
strings under 'prompts'. GENERATE THIS FIRST: the chosen render
is the reference image that video.json requires.
Built from PERSONALITY + GENDER only - NOTHING here is derived from the
tutor's display name, because names are placeholders that will be

the reverse. Gender and register are copied from tutor.md's documented

identity._heritage_note: a deliberate casting choice for a representative South African line-up; not inferred from any name
identity.build: petite and neat, poised, controlled precise gestures

face: oval face with a softly pointed chin, warm dark brown eyes with long lashes, olive-brown skin with golden undertone, gentle smile lines, small gold nose stud
hair: dark hair with a few silver strands, shoulder-length, pulled into a low neat bun with a centre parting

wardrobe.teaching: tailored blouse in teal or dusty rose under a fitted cardigan or neat blazer, dark straight-leg trousers, low heels
alternates: kurta-style tunic top for warmer, informal clips
blazer removed, sleeves buttoned, for board work

presence.posture: stands beside the document, highlighter poised, drawing the eye to one line at a time; small deliberate gestures
presence.default_expression: patient professional warmth, an encouraging nod, the look of someone who expects you to manage this
presence.energy: calm competence - makes real paperwork feel handleable

_environment_reference: bright practical classroom, an enlarged bill or plan pinned to the board, calculator and papers neatly arranged
_environment_note: NOT used for platform imagery - tutors are shot in studio. Owner, 2026-07-28: the student left the teachers in the classroom, so the platform does not show one. Kept only as character reference if a composite is ever wanted.
continuity_anchors: low neat bun with centre parting
_continuity_note: the features that MUST survive every regeneration - if these read the same, the audience accepts it as the same person

negative_prompt: cartoon, illustration, 3d render, cgi, airbrushed skin, waxy skin, plastic sheen, over-saturated colours, HDR halos, extra fingers, malformed hands, distorted ears, text, watermark, logo, subtitles, teeth artefacts, dead eyes, glassy doll eyes, vacant thousand-yard stare, identical catchlights in both eyes, flat matte irises, eyes looking through the camera, mismatched gaze direction, classroom, school desks, chalkboard, whiteboard, notice boards, posters, any writing or notation in frame, invented mathematical notation, holding two pieces of chalk, duplicated props, set dressing, generic stock-photo smile
_negative_note: the cinematic terms are deliberate - image models drift toward a film-still look (grade, motion blur, flare) and then the render stops reading as a photograph

headshot.lighting: large softbox key at 45 degrees, subtle hair light, seamless warm neutral grey studio backdrop
headshot.framing: chest-up, eyes on the upper third, slight three-quarter turn

studio.lighting: two-light studio set: large softbox key at 45 degrees, soft fill opposite, gentle rim light to lift the shoulders off the backdrop
studio.framing: waist-up, centred or slightly off-centre with clean space beside the head for overlaid text
studio.backdrop: seamless warm neutral grey paper, evenly lit, no props, no furniture, no set dressing

_anchor_rule: Anchors describe what is WORN or physically true of this person - never something held. An anchor is the strongest signal in this file, so a held object here puts it back in the hands whatever the prompt says.
_no_glasses: Owner 2026-07-29: no eyewear on this tutor. Five of twelve wore glasses, which flattened the line-up. The first accessory and the anchor were REPLACED rather than deleted - an empty slot lets the model invent something different every run.
_hands_rule: No held objects in any portrait prompt. The original generator inserted accessory #2 into a 'Holding one simple item' sentence regardless of whether it could be held, which is how a beaded wristband, a bangle, a watch and a pencil behind the ear all ended up 'held'. Objects belong in environment shots, on a surface.
_language_group_note: The cultural/language group this character belongs to. Recorded explicitly because it was previously only inferable from the surname, so a rename could change it silently. It does NOT alter the face - heritage drives appearance; language_group drives naming, and any traditional dress named in wardrobe.
objects: a municipal bill and a highlighter
_accessories_vs_objects: accessories = WORN ONLY, and portrait prompts may use them freely. objects = things this tutor teaches with; they belong in environment/classroom shots resting on a surface, and must NEVER enter a headshot or studio prompt. The two were one list, which is why held props kept reappearing: any template reaching into it could pull out a cash tin or a phone.
